user_reported_bug: Founder re-tested with the same bedroom photo from the original bug report — dark accent wall + wall art still not detected in the live app. Iteration 23 claimed 'fixed' but based only on unit tests (vocab-in-code assertions), never on a live image run. Investigation this round found: (1) `feature wall` DID fire in SAM3's raw output at 0.55–0.66 confidence — well above the 0.40 gate — but was being killed by the cross-class IoU dedup step because it overlaps almost-exactly with the plain `wall` detection at 0.83, so the higher-confidence `wall` wins. (2) `artwork`/`framed art`/`painting`/`picture frame` also fire strongly (0.75–0.96) and route to products by design (DETERMINISTIC_MATERIAL=None) — that's expected, not a bug. Fix: exempt semantic 'specialization' pairs (wall ↔ feature wall / accent wall / wainscot / paneled wainscoting / trim / backsplash; floor ↔ rug; bed ↔ headboard / pillow / cushion / mattress; sofa ↔ cushion / pillow) from cross-class IoU dedup so BOTH survive.
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Focused backend retest verified the actual live /api/projects/{id}/analyze flow with the requested Unsplash bedroom photo, not just unit tests. The response used real-scene-hybrid-v1 with no scene_fallback, returned 15 rows and 37 Stage-A objects, including 3 feature wall rows and 3 feature wall scene_stage_a objects (confidences 0.640625, 0.62109375, 0.5546875). The 31-test regression file also passed, covering both the specialization-pair dedup exemption and unrelated sink/mirror cross-class dedup.

Runtime evidence confirms the exemption now lets feature wall survive into both scene_stage_a and final analysis rows; artwork/framed art/picture frame also appear in Stage-A and remain product-routed as designed.
